column1: #A made-up multinomial logistic model for t/hirisplex.t, in the form
#trait_predict reads. Its betas are invented round numbers, NOT HIrisPlex-S's:
#those are not published, and Cn::Bioinf ships no model. What the test checks
#with it is the arithmetic and the bookkeeping, not anybody's prediction.
#A category with nothing but an intercept of 0 is the reference category,
#which is how a multinomial logistic model with k categories is written with
#k - 1 sets of betas. "(intercept)" stands in for a marker name. Markers are
#named as the webtool's CSV heads its columns, "<rs number>_<input allele>",
#which is how hirisplex_genotypes keys the genotypes it returns.
#eye uses two markers and hair_shade one, so that a trait whose markers are
#all present and one whose marker is missing are both covered; rs1805005_T is
#in no category, so the file also covers a marker the model names and the
#panel has, with a beta that only one trait uses.
